Sam (oncall): heads up: gpu attach backlog in us-central1, several pods stuck at Attaching >3m and k8s shows device busy errors :confused:
Nora (storage): looking at node traces, we had a badblock rewrite storm on a handful of nodes right when customers started provisioning. scrub triggered synchronous rewrite+fsync loops
Ibrahim (sre): did the rewrite originate from scrub or from an online recovery job? we saw a kernel oops a few hours ago on the same hosts
Nora (storage): the device-layer flagged transient read errors, our badblock handler scheduled rewrites. vendor fw also started a background block remap that made qdepth drop to 1
Jules (infra): any quick mitigation? we can't drain the entire pool, customer jobs are waiting
scrub-bot: auto-throttling badblock-rewrites on nodes tagged `gpu-hot` in us-central1 for 10m. reason: attach_pending>8 and device-qdepth<4 :zap:
Ibrahim (sre): nice. also suggest increasing attach timeout and bump local ioQuota to 1.5x on the affected nodepool to allow kubelet ops to finish
Sam (oncall): applying patch: `kubectl patch nodepool us-central-gpu --patch '{"spec":{"ioQuota":"150%"}}'` now. extending kubelet attach timeout via configmap
metrics-bot: device-qdepth median fell 64->3 at 01:12, host-local-io-latency p50 rose 6ms->180ms, attach_pending peaked 27
Nora (storage): long-term fixes: 1) make badblock handler do async remap + exponential backoff 2) mark nodes with active remap as low-priority for provisioning 3) ask vendor about firmware toggles to avoid remap during heavy attach windows
Ibrahim (sre): add to runbook: if badblock-rewrite rate >100/s and attach_pending>5 -> auto-throttle rewrites and bump ioQuota. also add an automated background fsck job after remap completes to clear stale metadata
Sam (oncall): backlog cleared after throttle + quota bump. keeping 30m watch. thanks all :thumbsup:
